title: Prove the conjugate-pair target needs four calls in every group (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Scoped written theorem in a formal group-algebra model, with a finite corroborating certificate. No new κ.**

For every group `G`, every field `F`, every pair `x, y ∈ G` with `xy ≠ yx` and every width `r ≥ 2`, the target `diag([xy],[yx],[e],…,[e])` in `M_r(F[G])` has exact paid-call minimum **four**. Paid factors are `I + ([g]-[e])N` with `g ∈ {x,y}` and `N` a rank-one idempotent, as in #4089.

This answers Open next question 2 of Wentao Li's #4089 (`research/a5-conjugate-any-registers`) for all conjugate-pair alphabets together. #4089 (A5) and #4093 (PSL(2,7)) rely on a support filter that is specific to each group. In a general group, coincidences such as `x²y = yx` defeat that filter, so the patterns `xxy`, `yyx`, `xyy` and `yxx` need a new argument.

New step ([PROOF.md](research/conjugate-pair-every-group/PROOF.md)): each factor is written as `[g]N + (I-N)`. Sandwiching a coefficient between `N_1` or `I-N_1` and `N_3` or `I-N_3` isolates one corner of call subsets. Three uniform lemmas follow:
1. the single-call products vanish;
2. the complementary corner of the `xy`/`yx` coefficients vanishes;
3. `P_{12}` and `P_{23}` cannot both be nonzero.

Every three-call pattern then fails, either by Lemma 3 or by a rank-one row/column mismatch. The proof uses no generation hypothesis, element order or field characteristic. For `y = x⁻¹` the target is `I`, so the noncommuting hypothesis is necessary.

## Evidence and reproduction

`verify.py` checks the following:
- The expansion and corner identities, on 200 seeded rational triples.
- 82 distinct length-4 coincidence signatures of noncommuting pairs in S3, S4, S5, Q8 and the free group. The direct four-call word and all four one-call deletions are checked on each.
- Exhaustive exclusion of every word of length 1..3. These words fall into 26 subset-class keys. All are checked over F2 at widths 2 and 3 and over F3 at width 2.
- The inverse-pair control.

The finite check corroborates the proof. It does not cover all groups or widths.

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B -W error research/conjugate-pair-every-group/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -B -W error research/conjugate-pair-every-group/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/conjugate-pair-every-group
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/conjugate-pair-every-group --check-source-history
```

All four commands passed locally on head `0cee0e104b68ce6f06bf84af03f46ac30680e64c`, base `19fdb086ea96af9a9f87936a2b888e10af4ed810`. Markers were `PASS_CONJUGATE_PAIR_EVERY_GROUP`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Each verifier run takes about 5 s.

## Limitations

- The theorem holds only in the formal group-algebra model. No native address operation, conversion, restoration or recursive caller is priced, and this is not a multiplication theorem.
- The selected κ is unchanged.
- The written proof has had no independent human review and no proof-kernel check.
- The results of #4089, #4093 and #2246 are cited, not re-checked.

## Open next questions

1. Which pair targets `diag([g],[h])` in an arbitrary group allow cross-register sharing below the sum of their positive word lengths? Corner sandwiches might give uniform floors in place of per-group censuses. A first step is `diag([xyx],[yxy])` at length five.
2. Does an admitted BIT supplier have a priced native nonabelian address alphabet? This theorem rules out any saving on this target in every group, so such a proposal has to find its gain elsewhere.

## Related open work

No open PR studies this target or the general-group conjugate-pair floor.

- #6039 (opened after this PR's claim) works in the same rank-one-idempotent group-algebra model over F2[Q8], but on a different target: the mixed shape of four `[zi]` and one `[zj]` targets. Its target is not computed here, so there are no numbers to compare.
